text:
acme-corp (customer): Hey team — since yesterday afternoon we're getting a lot of 429s from the on-prem gateway after our nightly batch. It looks like a sudden burst (cron job spikes to ~1200 rps for a few mins). Gateway is customer-managed in our VPC. No code changes on our side.

acme-corp (customer): Sample gateway log lines: 
`2025-12-02T02:11:13Z WARN rate_limiter: rate limit exceeded user=svc-account-123 route=/generate 429`
`2025-12-02T02:11:14Z ERROR upstream: 503 upstream reset`

lena (support): Sorry you're seeing that — we can help. A few quick questions: which gateway are you running (nginx-ingress / envoy / ambassador)? K8s version? Also paste your ingress annotations and the gateway ConfigMap if possible.

acme-corp (customer): We're on nginx-ingress (kubernetes/ingress-nginx controller v1.9.1), k8s 1.25. Ingress has these annotations: `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "50"` and `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-burst-multiplier: "1"` (we copied defaults from our old infra). Our gateway is in a small node pool (2x vCPU, 8GB).

josh (sre): That rps annotation is per-IP by default and low for a bursty batch job. Two quick paths: 1) increase burst/token bucket size on the ingress controller or 2) put a short-lived rollout to route batch traffic through a different route with higher limits.

josh (sre): Can you run these so we can repro locally:
```
# from inside cluster (or a pod with curl)
kubectl -n ingress-nginx get configmap nginx-configuration -o yaml
kubectl -n ingress-nginx logs deploy/ingress-nginx-controller --tail=200 | grep rate
```
And from your dev machine: `hey -z 60s -c 200 http://<gateway-ip>/generate` to simulate the nightly spike.

acme-corp (customer): Ran the configmap. Key bits: `limit-rps: "50"`, `limit-rpm: "3000"`, rate-limiting is enabled via the lua module. Logs attached show many `token bucket empty` messages. We can run the hey test; planning to do it during a maintenance window.

anika (runtime): If logs say token bucket empty that's the limiter hitting capacity. For nginx-ingress lua limiters you need to tune both the refill size and the burst. Example adjusted annotation (on the Ingress or via ConfigMap) we recommend for short high-burst jobs: 
```yaml
metadata:
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "200"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-burst-multiplier: "4"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-whitelist: "10.11.12.0/24,10.11.13.0/24"  # if you want to exempt internal batch jobs by source
```
Note: `limit-burst-multiplier` multiplies the base token bucket to allow short bursts.

anika (runtime): If you're using Envoy rate-limit service instead, modify the token_bucket config. Example envoy RLS token bucket YAML: 
```yaml
rate_limits:
  - actions:
      - request_headers:
          header_name: x-api-key
    stage: 0
token_bucket:
  max_tokens: 500
  tokens_per_fill: 50
  fill_interval_ms: 1000
```
This gives a bigger bucket to absorb a 10s spike at high rps.

lena (support): Short-term mitigation steps we usually recommend: 1) whitelist batch job pod IPs (via whitelist annotation) so they skip per-IP limits, 2) bump burst/multiplier in ingress config and restart controller, 3) scale gateway pods to increase aggregate capacity.

acme-corp (customer): We can try whitelisting, but our batch runs from many ephemeral pods across nodes so IP ranges are large. Is there a way to whitelist by service account or header?

josh (sre): Yes — you can set a header in the batch job (e.g., `X-Internal-Batch: true`) and then add a rule in nginx to skip limiter when that header is present, or use Envoy route-specific rate limits keyed by header. Example nginx snippet (ConfigMap/custom template): 
```
if ($http_x_internal_batch = "true") {
  set $limit 0;
}
```
Not ideal but fine for controlled batch traffic.

infra-bot: :eyes: Incident created: INC-2025-412 (internal tracking). Assigned to josh (sre).

lena (support): Also FYI — because this is a customer-managed gateway, we can't bump control-plane quotas from Redwood side, but we can help generate a safe patch you can apply. If you'd like, we can prepare a patch to: increase limit-rps to 200, set burst-multiplier to 4, and add an example header-exempt rule. Want us to draft that?

acme-corp (customer): Yes please. Also would appreciate a minimal repro we can run to validate changes before prod.

anika (runtime): Draft patch below (apply to your ingress-nginx ConfigMap or as annotations on the Ingress). After applying, do `kubectl -n ingress-nginx rollout restart deploy/ingress-nginx-controller` to pick up changes. 
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: nginx-configuration
  namespace: ingress-nginx
data:
  limit-rps: "200"
  limit-burst-multiplier: "4"
  limit-whitelist: "10.11.0.0/16"  # optional
  server-tokens: "false"
```
And add this to your batch job pod spec env / curl headers: `-H "X-Internal-Batch: true"`.

anika (runtime): Quick local repro using hey: `hey -z 30s -c 300 -H "X-Internal-Batch: false" http://<gateway>/generate` should show 429s. Then flip header to true to verify exemptions.

acme-corp (customer): Applied patch in staging and did the hey test. Before: 40% 429s. After: almost 0 429s and p95 latency improved. Rolling to prod tonight. Huge help, thank you. :tada:

devon (sales): Nice — tagging this as resolved from onboarding perspective once prod roll completes. If you want an efficiency review later we can look at right-sizing node pool and autoscaling to save cost.

josh (sre): Follow-ups for us (anika + josh): 1) add a short doc to support playbook for private/VPC rate-limit tuning (nginx vs envoy), 2) consider adding a template for header-based whitelisting, 3) investigate SRE-side detection to surface "burst vs sustained" patterns to customers.

anika (runtime): I'll add a runbook and include the example Envoy token_bucket and nginx annotations. Will post PR to docs later today.

lena (support): Closing the thread once acme confirms prod stable. If anything reappears ping me. :+1:

acme-corp (customer): Prod roll is done, no new 429s during the scheduled spike window. Thanks everyone, closing from our side.
